logicalBugs.description: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Open the Actions page for a model saved in a personal collection; actions are forms that run SQL against that model’s database. Its location breadcrumb says “Our analytics” instead of the personal collection containing the model, although the model itself was not moved.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ModelActions uses a separate loaded model container from the query builder; the navigation breadcrumb falls back to root collection context instead of using the loaded model collection. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A model is a reusable saved query displayed as a table or list, with configurable column labels and formatting. Open the Actions page for a model saved in a personal collection; actions are forms that run SQL against that model’s database. Its location breadcrumb says “Our analytics” instead of the personal collection containing the model, although the model itself was not moved.

logicalBugs.description: Data Reference is a catalog of database tables and columns, with descriptions, related records and suggested questions for exploring their data. The supplied Orders table’s ID description calls it a product identifier even though Orders has its own row ID and a separate Product ID. The reference text describes the wrong kind of record; the stored IDs need not be incorrect.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The sample-data field record contains an incorrect description, consumed directly by the reference/metadata UI. The upstream frontend cannot establish the original seeded record or authoring location. The exact cause remains unresolved. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Data Reference is a catalog of database tables and columns, with descriptions, related records and suggested questions for exploring their data. The supplied Orders table’s ID description calls it a product identifier even though Orders has its own row ID and a separate Product ID. The reference text describes the wrong kind of record; the stored IDs need not be incorrect.

logicalBugs.description: Questions are saved queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved aggregate calculations. Each has a title, a collection location and revision history. Opening History on a dashboard, model or metric can show “undefined modified this” where the person’s name should be. The observable failure is the literal missing-name text in an existing revision entry, not the absence of history or a claim that an unauthorized actor edited the item.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Timeline revision copy reads r.user.common_name directly for another actor, without reconstructing a name or providing a fallback when the seeded revision user lacks that property. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A metric is a saved calculation such as a count or average. Open History on a supplied metric: an existing revision says “undefined modified this” instead of naming its author or using a neutral fallback.

A model is a reusable saved query presented as a table or list. Open History on a supplied model: an existing revision says “undefined modified this” instead of identifying who made the change. This is missing author text, not missing revision history.

logicalBugs.description: The embedding wizard configures how a saved question or dashboard is displayed outside Metabase, including a live preview and initial or locked filter values. With German selected, the metric-embedding setup sentence leaves the English word “question” or its untranslated substitution in the displayed text. The language error is in the setup explanation, not a failed embed or a changed metric type.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The German translation for the embed question/type interpolation does not substitute the intended resource label. The relevant locale string is not proved by the component alone. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A metric is a saved calculation that can be embedded outside Metabase. Set the interface language to German and open metric embedding setup. The parameter guidance retains the English word “question” in “Dieses question hat noch keine konfigurierbaren Parameter” rather than translating the item description.

logicalBugs.description: A model created from an uploaded CSV file can receive more rows by append or replace all of its existing uploaded rows with another file. A successful CSV append or replacement produces a notification whose filename link opens a blank new question instead of the updated model. The upload itself succeeds; the broken destination is the link in its success message.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The upload notification constructs a model link from the upload result while append/replace responses do not supply the same model identifier as new-model creation. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: An uploaded-CSV model is a saved table-like view of the uploaded data. Successfully append or replace its rows, then click the filename link in the success notification. It leads to /model/undefined and a blank New question rather than the updated model; the upload itself succeeded.

logicalBugs.description: A metric is a saved, reusable aggregate such as a count or average; its definition chooses source data, filters, formula and an optional date grouping for showing changes over time. Attempt to save a new metric before selecting its starting data. The failure exposes a raw DATABASE_ID database constraint and SQL INSERT text instead of identifying the missing source in the editor.
logicalBugs.rootCause: MetricEditorHeader disables Save changes for saved metrics using !isRunnable||!isDirty, but its new-metric Save button has no disabled/isRunnable condition. It therefore opens creation/save for an incomplete metric with no database/source. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A metric is a saved calculation such as a count or average, optionally grouped by a date. Attempt to save a new metric before selecting its starting data. The failure exposes a raw DATABASE_ID database constraint and SQL INSERT text instead of identifying the missing source in the editor.

logicalBugs.description: A model created from an uploaded CSV file can receive more rows by append or replace all of its existing uploaded rows with another file. Replace an already populated uploaded model with a CSV containing an invalid number or date. Validation reports failure, but the old rows have already been deleted instead of being preserved when the replacement cannot complete; this differs from a successful replacement intentionally removing previous rows.
logicalBugs.rootCause: update-with-csv! calls driver/truncate! before driver/insert-into! in a try/catch without a transaction/rollback, so an insert failure leaves the original rows already deleted. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A model is a reusable saved query. An uploaded-CSV model already contains saved rows. Choose Replace with a file containing an invalid number or date: the upload reports a parsing error, but reopening the model shows no rows because its earlier data was deleted. This is failure to preserve data after a rejected replacement, not the intended removal during a successful replacement.

logicalBugs.description: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Restore an earlier model revision or change an upstream model’s returned columns, then compare the result table with More info > Overview. The table uses the restored/new fields, but Overview lists old names, an old count or removed columns instead of describing the data currently returned.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Overview SidesheetCardWithFields derives fields from Lib.returnedColumns(question.query(),-1), not the newly executed dataset response. If a revert or upstream source change leaves the query metadata provider stale, the field list retains its previous columns despite updated result data. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A model is a reusable saved query with an Info > Overview list of its columns. Restore an earlier model revision after renaming or removing a column. The table restores the earlier names and columns, but Overview keeps the newer names or incomplete field list rather than describing the restored results.

A model is a reusable saved query. Build one saved model from another model, then change the source model’s returned column from AMOUNT to BALANCE. The dependent model’s results correctly show BALANCE, but Info > Overview continues listing the removed AMOUNT column. The failure is the dependent model’s column description, not its returned data.

logicalBugs.description: In Metabase, a model is a saved query used as a table-like data source, and a metric is a saved calculation such as a sum. Restoring one from Trash, or restoring an earlier query definition through Info → History, can leave the open editor and information panel inconsistent with the restored saved item. Depending on the path, editing still uses the Trash location, the source link is absent, the definition refers to the item itself, or an existing bookmark appears inactive. The data or restored item can be present while these controls still describe an earlier state; the affected restore workflow and visible discrepancy must match.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Restore updates the entity record but leaves the query-builder card/original-card and collection/source metadata stale; editing, bookmarks and Overview continue to use the archived/self-referencing representation until reinitialization. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A metric is a saved calculation. A model is a reusable saved query. Restore an open model or metric from Trash, then use that same page without reloading. Renaming or converting it can show a permission error, and Duplicate can remain disabled despite valid inputs. Reloading makes those operations work; the problem follows the completed Restore rather than an actual lack of permission.

A model is a reusable saved query. Its Overview should identify the table supplying its data under Based on. Change its source from Products to People, save, then use History to restore the earlier Products revision. Products rows return, but Overview loses the Based on section instead of linking to Products. This path restores a revision, not an item from Trash.

A metric is a saved calculation. A model is a reusable saved query. Restore a saved model or metric from Trash and open its query-definition editor before refreshing the page. A model can list itself as its source instead of its original table; a metric can replace its original formula with its own name and omit a saved filter. Further editing can fail to save, while refresh restores the correct definition.

A model is a reusable saved query. Bookmark a saved model, move it to Trash and restore it, then open it through the retained sidebar bookmark. The model toolbar shows the unfilled Bookmark icon as though it were not bookmarked, although that sidebar bookmark still exists.

logicalBugs.description: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Rename a calculated model output or replace its source so that the output columns change. Saved display names, descriptions and data-role choices can be discarded or attached to a different new expression, leaving labels that no longer describe the returned values instead of keeping each column’s customizations with the correct output.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Model edit patches are keyed by focusedFieldName; Question.setResultMetadataDiff later applies each patch only through metadataDiff[column.name]. Renaming/replacing an output changes that identity, so saved per-column patches no longer attach to the renamed output or attach to a reused source name. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A column in a model (a reusable saved query) can have a custom display name, description and data role such as Currency. Rename a calculated output in the model’s query without changing the calculation. Saving discards those custom settings: the display name falls back to the new expression name, the description empties and the data role resets.

A model is a reusable saved query. Save a model based on Orders, then change its source to People without editing column labels. The results contain people’s names but the name column keeps the unrelated User ID label from Orders, including after refresh. The error is an inherited label attached to the wrong new output.

logicalBugs.description: A model is a saved, table-like query that can show records as a list and open a single row in a detail view. An entity key is the column whose value identifies that record for search and navigation. Configure a column’s link URL or displayed link text to include another column’s value, such as an ID placeholder. Model tables can substitute that value correctly, but record details and administrative previews leave it empty even when the referenced value is visible in the same record; a placeholder for the current column can still work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Detail-view renderValue builds both visualization columns and clicked.data from only the current column/value. Cross-column template placeholders therefore lack the rest of the row, although table results format the same settings correctly. The report also observes the admin Table preview; its separate row construction is not established by this reference. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A model (a reusable saved query) can display a column as a link whose URL contains another column’s value, such as {{ID}}. The table correctly fills in the ID, but opening that row’s popup or full-page details drops the ID from the same URL even though it is visible on the record. This concerns the link destination, not the displayed link text.

A model is a reusable saved query whose columns can display links with custom text. Configure link text to include another column’s value, such as Product followed by its ID. The model table shows that value, but the selected record’s details omit it and show only Product. This concerns the displayed link label, not the link destination.

logicalBugs.description: A metric is a saved, reusable aggregate such as a count or average; its definition chooses source data, filters, formula and an optional date grouping for showing changes over time. Add or change a metric’s default date column/grouping and save. The page can temporarily show a date as the metric’s single value instead of its aggregate-over-time chart, while changing only Month to Year can leave Save disabled and retain the old result; refresh can restore the correct visualization.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Default-time settings update the metric visualization/query representation without synchronizing the editor dirty/results metadata state; the date column can be rendered as the scalar until reload and a bucket-only change may not enable Save. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A metric is a saved calculation such as Count, optionally grouped by a date. Add a default date grouping and save: the result temporarily becomes a single large date even though multiple result rows exist, hiding the calculated values. Reloading displays the expected Count-over-time chart.

A metric (a saved calculation) can group its calculation by a chosen date interval. Change its existing default grouping from Month to Year. The selection chip says Year, but Save changes remains disabled and the displayed result still uses Month, preventing the interval change from being saved.

logicalBugs.description: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Convert between question, model and metric, then use the offered Undo action. It can leave the converted type unchanged, restore the model UI under an unsaved-question URL, or lose saved column names/descriptions/types even after reload, instead of restoring the complete prior item.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Conversion and undo update card type through the query-builder save flow, but the undo snapshot omits/restores stale display settings, result_metadata or route state. This loses model URL and custom metadata across conversions. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A metric is a saved calculation; a model is a reusable table-like query. Convert a metric to a model and click the offered Undo. The conversion remains in effect and the item stays absent from Browse Metrics after reload instead of returning to its original metric type.

A model is a reusable saved query. Convert a saved model with a configured List view into a saved question, then click Undo. The named model interface returns, but the address remains an unsaved-question URL. Reloading that address opens a blank New question editor instead of the saved model, which still exists separately.

A model (a reusable saved query) can store custom column labels, descriptions and data roles. Convert it to a saved question and use Undo to return to the model. Its columns revert to source defaults and lose their custom settings, including after reload, rather than restoring the model’s complete prior configuration.

logicalBugs.description: Data Reference can display a segment, which is a saved reusable row filter, and offer links to questions using that definition. Open or reload a segment’s Data Reference detail after the segment was retired or is no longer available. The page crashes with an unhandled “reading table_id” error and can show incomplete links instead of a useful missing/retired-segment page.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SegmentDetailContainer requires segment and passes it to SegmentSidebar/SegmentDetail without a loading/not-found guard. A missing or retired segment can reach selectors/rendering that access table_id. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A segment is a saved reusable filter listed in Data Reference, Metabase’s database catalog. Leave a segment’s reference page open, retire the segment and reload that page. It shows a blank title and an unhandled error mentioning table_id instead of useful retired/unavailable information; its See this segment link can also be incomplete.

A segment is a saved reusable filter whose definition can be opened in Data Reference. Navigate to the reported segment’s reference detail page. The main content displays “Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'table_id')” rather than details or a useful unavailable message. This path does not establish retirement as its prerequisite.

logicalBugs.description: Questions are saved queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved aggregate calculations. Each has a title, a collection location and revision history. Rename the item directly in its page header to a string containing only spaces. The header becomes blank without validation feedback even though saving is rejected, and reopening restores the old name; an exactly empty title can take a different, correctly reverting path.
logicalBugs.rootCause: EditableText treats a nonempty whitespace string as a submitted value, and SavedQuestionLeftSide only checks name truthiness before saving. The locally committed text remains visible when the server rejects a blank trimmed name; an exactly empty value takes the separate revert branch. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A metric is a named saved calculation. Edit its title directly in the page header, replace the name with spaces only and press Enter. The title becomes visually blank without validation feedback even though saving is rejected; reloading restores the old name. An exactly empty name correctly reverts immediately.

A model is a named reusable saved query. Rename it in its page header to spaces only and press Enter. The header remains blank without an error, but leaving and reopening restores the saved name. This is a rejected item-title edit displayed as blank, not a whitespace column label that actually saves.

logicalBugs.description: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Edit a model column’s display name and then quickly edit its description before the first change finishes saving. The description update cancels or overwrites the pending name edit, so saving both controls loses the name change rather than keeping the two independent fields.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DatasetFieldMetadataSidebar creates one debounced onFieldMetadataChange shared by handleDisplayNameChange and handleDescriptionChange. A description change inside 500ms replaces the pending name change rather than merging the patches. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.

logicalBugs.description: Questions are saved queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved aggregate calculations. Each has a title, a collection location and revision history. Move an open saved item to Trash and inspect its red archive banner. Restore and Delete permanently are missing until reload, even for a user allowed to use those actions; this is missing immediate recovery controls, not a failed Restore click.

ViewHeaderContainer passes card.can_restore and card.can_delete directly to the banner, so the pre-trash permissions can hide Restore/Delete until a full reload supplies the archived card. The exact mutation response in the unavailable fixture revision remains unverified. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Saved questions are queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved calculations; each has a name and revision history. Move an open saved item to Trash and inspect its red archive banner. Restore and Delete permanently are missing until reload, even for a user allowed to use those actions; this is missing immediate recovery controls, not a failed Restore click.

logicalBugs.description: Questions are saved queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved aggregate calculations. The list returns to the document icon instead of retaining the selected icon, even though the other layout changes may be saved.

Clicking its displayed value opens the model’s record-details panel instead of following the configured link, unlike an ordinary linked column.
